\]

\[
\mu = \frac{m_e m_e}{m_e+m_e} = \frac{m_e}{2}\;\;\Longrightarrow\;\; \frac{\mu}{m_e} = \frac12 .
\]

Hence  

\[
E_n = -\frac{13.6\,\text{eV}}{2n^2}= -\frac{6.8\,\text{eV}}{n^2}.
\]

Calculate the energies of the \(n=3\) and \(n=1\) levels:

\[
E_3 = -\frac{6.8}{9}\,\text{eV}\approx -0.756\,\text{eV},\qquad
E_1 = -6.8\,\text{eV}.
\]

The photon energy emitted in the transition \(n=3 \to n=1\) is

\[
\Delta E = E_1 - E_3 = (-6.8) - (-0.756)\,\text{eV}\approx 6.04\,\text{eV},
\]

which is closest to 6.0 eV.
